items.prompt: White to move. Only one move wins. Find the move that takes the opposition.
hints: Where should the white king stand so that Black's king must move away first?
Put the king directly in front of the pawn, facing Black's king with exactly one square between them.
The king goes to e5; then Black is the one who must move.
items.explain: Ke5 puts the kings face to face with one square between and leaves Black to move. The tablebase shows Ke5 wins and every other White move here (the pawn push or any other king step) only draws.

feedback_by_move.e4e5: Pushing the pawn lets Black answer Kd7 or Kd8 and the game is a draw: the pawn needs the king in front of it first.
feedback_by_move.d5d4: Stepping back lets Black come forward; the tablebase shows a draw.
feedback_by_move.d5c6: The king leaves the pawn's file and Black holds the draw.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's king is in front of the pawn, one square between the kings. With best play, what is the result?
hints: Look at who has to move.
Each Black king move gives way; can Black stay opposite the white king?
Black cannot keep the facing position: every move loses.
items.explain: Black must leave the facing square, and the tablebase gives White the win after each of Black's five legal moves.

items.prompt: The same position, but now it is White's move. With best play, what is the result?
hints: Compare with the last position: only the side to move has changed.
Can White make a useful king move without giving Black the facing position?
White has no move that keeps the advantage.
items.explain: With White to move the same position is a draw: the tablebase confirms that each of White's four legal king moves only draws.

items.prompt: Everything shifted one file to the left. Black to move. What is the result?
hints: Which parts of the picture are the same as the first position?
The pawn is still not a rook pawn.
Same pattern, same result.
items.explain: Moving the whole picture one file to the left changes nothing here: the tablebase gives the same result as for the e-file.

items.prompt: Black to move again, and the pawn is still on e4. But White's king stands on d5, not e5. What is the result?
hints: Are the kings still facing each other with one square between?
Black has one move that keeps the kings facing.
Black plays Kd7 and the kings face on the d-file with White to move.
items.explain: From d5 White is not in front of the pawn's file. Black's only drawing move is Kd7, after which the kings face each other with White to move; the other four Black moves lose.

items.prompt: The pawn has moved back to e3; the kings are as in the first position. Black to move. What is the result?
hints: Only the pawn's rank is different.
The white king is still in front of the pawn.
The result is the same as with the pawn on e4.
items.explain: With the pawn two squares from the start the tablebase still gives White the win when Black must move; moving the pawn back does not change the result here.

items.prompt: Black to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Compare the rank of the white king with the rank of the pawn.
Is the white king in front of the pawn or level with it?
Black plays Ke6 and the pawn can go no further.
items.explain: The kings face each other and Black is to move, but White's king is level with the pawn, not ahead of it. Black's only drawing move is Ke6; the other four lose, and the tablebase gives a draw.

items.prompt: White to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Look at where the white king stands compared with the pawn.
The white king is two ranks in front of the pawn.
White wins even though he has to move.
items.explain: The kings face each other, yet it is White who must move, and the tablebase still gives White the win: the king is on e6, two ranks in front of the e4 pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Which file is the pawn on?
A pawn on the edge file has fewer squares to run to.
Black's king can stay in the corner region.
items.explain: The pawn is on the a-file and Black's king stays near the corner. With Black to move the tablebase gives a draw, and both of Black's legal moves keep it.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a winning move (more than one wins).
hints: Think about which rank the king must reach.
The winning moves put the king two ranks in front of the pawn.
Ke6, Kd6 or Kf6.
items.explain: Each of Ke6, Kd6 and Kf6 reaches the sixth rank in front of the pawn, and the tablebase shows all three win. The four other king moves draw.

feedback_by_move.e5d5: Staying level with the pawn gives Black time: the tablebase shows a draw.
feedback_by_move.e5d4: Stepping back does not make progress: draw.
feedback_by_move.e5f5: Staying level with the pawn gives Black time: draw.

items.prompt: The same position, but Black is to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Compare with the previous position: only the side to move changed.
Can Black take the facing position now?
Black plays Ke7 and White cannot make progress.
items.explain: With Black to move the position is a draw: the tablebase shows Black's only drawing reply is Ke7, which leaves the kings facing each other with White to move. The same setup wins for White when White is to move.

items.prompt: White to move. Only one move wins. Which?
hints: Where should the king stand to make Black move first?
Put the king in front of the pawn with one square between the kings.
Ke4.
items.explain: Ke4 faces Black's king with one square between and Black to move; every Black reply then loses, while all four other White moves draw.

feedback_by_move.e3e4: Pushing the pawn first lets Black take the facing position: draw.
feedback_by_move.d4c4: The king leaves the pawn's file: draw.
feedback_by_move.d4d3: A step back loses time: draw.

items.prompt: You are White. Win this ending against the best defence. Remember the first move.

claims.statement: The goal (win) is achievable: the tablebase result for the side to move is a win.

hints: The first move decides: the pawn can wait.
After Ke5 keep your king in front of the pawn until it can run.
Go forward with the king, push the pawn only when it is safe.
items.explain: The tablebase says White wins from here; the only first move that keeps the win is Ke5.

items.prompt: You are Black. Hold the draw against the best play. One first move holds; the others lose.

claims.statement: The goal (hold) is achievable: the tablebase result for the side to move is a draw.

hints: Which of your five king moves keeps your king facing White's?
Your king must stay in front of the pawn's path.
Kd7 is the only move that holds.
items.explain: The tablebase says Black can draw from here and that Kd7 is the only drawing first move.
